nodes.description: Two pathogenic TULP1 alleles in trans or in homozygosity. Allele classes include nonsense and frameshift variants (the Arabian p.Gln301Ter and the Finnish c.148delG founder alleles), canonical splice-site variants that produce frameshifted transcripts, a small in-frame duplication, and missense variants that cluster in the conserved C-terminal tubby domain. TULP1 is expressed in rod and cone photoreceptors, so the primary lesion sits in both cell types.

evidence.reference_title: Novel TULP1 mutation causing leber congenital amaurosis or early onset retinal degeneration.
evidence.snippet: Linkage analysis identified a region of homozygosity on chromosome 6, region p21.3, and mutation screening revealed a novel 6-base in-frame duplication, in the TULP1 gene.

evidence.reference_title: A TULP1 founder mutation, p.Gln301*, underlies a recognisable congenital rod-cone dystrophy phenotype on the Arabian Peninsula.
evidence.snippet: The TULP1 allele p.Gln301* represents a founder mutation on the Arabian Peninsula and is associated with a recognisable congenital recessive rod-cone dystrophy phenotype in the homozygous state.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic Variants in TULP1 Are Associated with Heterogeneous Phenotypes of Retinal Dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Seventeen different alleles were identified, namely eight missense variants, six nonsense variants, one in-frame deletion variant, and two splice site variants.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal degeneration in tulp1-/- mice: vesicular accumulation in the interphotoreceptor matrix.
evidence.snippet: The function of Tulp1 is required to maintain viability of rod and cone photoreceptors.

nodes.description: A bull's eye maculopathy is reported in the homozygous splice-site kindred, in patients with the p.Arg420Ser allele, and as an isolated finding in two siblings with compound heterozygous missense alleles.

evidence.snippet: Homozygotes had nystagmus, visual acuity of 20/200 or worse, color vision disturbances, bull's eye maculopathy, and peripheral pigmentary retinopathy.

evidence.reference_title: Maternal uniparental isodisomy of chromosome 6 reveals a TULP1 mutation as a novel cause of cone dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: Both patients carrying the p.Arg420Ser mutation presented with a bull's eye maculopathy.

nodes.description: Cones are involved early in Tulp1-null mice, together with rods. In patients, cone electroretinograms are reduced and delayed in early childhood and lost on repeat testing years later, leaving a small central island of foveal cones. Because TULP1 is expressed in cones and the cone-expressed zebrafish paralog is needed for cone opsin targeting and cone survival, cone loss is treated here as at least partly primary.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal degeneration in tulp1-/- mice: vesicular accumulation in the interphotoreceptor matrix.
evidence.snippet: Photoreceptor degeneration developed in tulp1-/- mice, with early involvement of both rods and cones.

evidence.reference_title: A TULP1 founder mutation, p.Gln301*, underlies a recognisable congenital rod-cone dystrophy phenotype on the Arabian Peninsula.
evidence.snippet: Rod function was non-recordable while cone function was present (albeit depressed and delayed); however, repeat electroretinogram years later in two children revealed loss of recordable cone function.

evidence.snippet: Retinal degeneration with TULP1 mutations leads to a small central island of residual foveal cones at early ages.

nodes.description: Electron microscopy of Tulp1-null retina shows massive accumulation of extracellular vesicles around the distal inner segments, in the interphotoreceptor matrix. The vesicles contain rhodopsin. This is not a general feature of photoreceptor degeneration; it is shared with only a small group of models, and it is the ultrastructural signature of misdirected opsin transport.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal degeneration in tulp1-/- mice: vesicular accumulation in the interphotoreceptor matrix.
evidence.snippet: Electron microscopy revealed massive accumulation of extracellular vesicles surrounding the distal inner segments.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal degeneration in tulp1-/- mice: vesicular accumulation in the interphotoreceptor matrix.
evidence.snippet: Extracellular vesicular accumulation is not a common phenomenon associated with photoreceptor degeneration but appears to be a distinct ultrastructural feature shared by a small group of retinal disease models.

nodes.description: In light, arrestin normally moves from the inner to the outer segment to quench activated rhodopsin. In Tulp1-null photoreceptors it does not. This is a soluble-protein movement, distinct from the two membrane carrier pathways, and its consequence for the light response in TULP1 disease has not been measured.

evidence.reference_title: Immunocytochemical evidence of Tulp1-dependent outer segment protein transport pathways in photoreceptor cells.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, arrestin does not translocate to the outer segment in response to light stimulation.

nodes.description: In Tulp1-null photoreceptors before degeneration, retinal guanylate cyclase 1 and its activating proteins GCAP1 and GCAP2 are mislocalized, while phosphodiesterase, which does not share their carrier vesicles, is not. This is a second integral-membrane outer segment carrier pathway, separate from the opsin pathway, that depends on TULP1.

biological_processes: protein localization to photoreceptor outer segment

evidence.reference_title: Immunocytochemical evidence of Tulp1-dependent outer segment protein transport pathways in photoreceptor cells.
evidence.snippet: These data implicate Tulp1 in the transport of selective integral membrane outer segment proteins and their associated proteins, specifically, the opsin and guanylate cyclase carrier pathways.

nodes.description: Two independent case reports describe a distinctive perivascular pattern: increased autofluorescence along the retinal vessels with periarteriolar pigmentation, alongside a bull's eye maculopathy. It is reported in biallelic missense and splice genotypes, not in the truncating founder series, so it is recorded without a frequency.

evidence.snippet: We identified two TULP1 gene variants in a patient exhibiting unusual and symmetrical alterations in both retinas, characterized by an increase in autofluorescence along the distribution of retinal vessels.

evidence.reference_title: TULP1 related retinal dystrophy: report of rare and novel variants with a previously undescribed phenotype in two cases.
evidence.snippet: In both patients, a unique pattern of perivascular retinal degeneration was noted.

evidence.reference_title: TULP1 related retinal dystrophy: report of rare and novel variants with a previously undescribed phenotype in two cases.
evidence.snippet: Patients with TULP1-related retinal dystrophy can have a distinctive retinopathy with a unique pattern of macular degeneration and periarteriolar vascular pigmentation.

evidence.reference_title: Tubby-like protein 1 homozygous splice-site mutation causes early-onset severe retinal degeneration.
evidence.snippet: This TULP1 splice-site mutation in homozygotes causes early-onset, severe retinal degeneration involving macular and peripheral cones and rods.

nodes.description: TULP1 is weakly expressed in some inner nuclear layer and ganglion cells, and Tulp1-null retinas show bipolar, amacrine and ganglion cell changes not seen in rhodopsin- or Rds-null retinas, suggesting that part of the inner retinal involvement is primary rather than remodelling after photoreceptor loss. Patients show inner retinal thickening. Whether this is primary is unresolved, and it matters for photoreceptor-targeted gene therapy.

evidence.snippet: While common features of photoreceptor degeneration were detected in Tulp1-/-, Rho-/-, and Rds-/- retinas, other alterations in bipolar, amacrine and ganglion cells were specific to Tulp1-/- mice.

nodes.description: At the photoreceptor terminal, TULP1 is concentrated in the periactive zone beside the synaptic ribbon, together with dynamin-1 and other endocytic proteins. Without TULP1 the endocytic proteins are no longer enriched there and endocytic activity near the ribbon falls, which would impair the vesicle recycling that sustained ribbon-synapse release depends on.

evidence.reference_title: The Disease Protein Tulp1 Is Essential for Periactive Zone Endocytosis in Photoreceptor Ribbon Synapses.
evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that Tulp1 is highly enriched in the periactive zone of photoreceptor presynaptic terminals where Tulp1 colocalizes with major endocytic proteins close to the synaptic ribbon.

nodes.description: Null alleles remove TULP1 protein, and the Tulp1 knockout mouse reproduces early-onset rod and cone degeneration. TULP1 is a soluble, roughly 70 kDa cytoplasmic protein that associates with membranes, probably through phosphorylated phospholipids, and binds F-actin and the GTPase dynamin-1. It colocalizes with actin at the inner segment, connecting cilium and outer limiting membrane and with dynamin-1 at the synaptic terminal, which places it in vesicular trafficking at both ends of the cell. TUB and TULP1 do not substitute for one another.

nodes.description: In patients, photoreceptor function is lost earlier and more completely than photoreceptor structure. Rod function is unmeasurable at every age examined, including in children whose central OCT is normal and in young LCA patients whose fundus looks virtually normal, and the central island of surviving foveal cones is less sensitive than its preserved laminar thickness predicts. Which TULP1-dependent defect accounts for this is not settled; misrouted opsin and cyclase in the outer segment and a malformed ribbon synapse are the candidates from the mouse.

This is the TULP1-specific form of the module's photoreceptor stress node; oxidative stress has not been examined in TULP1 models.

nodes.description: Tulp1-null photoreceptor terminals develop with few intact synaptic ribbons, and the ribbon-associated proteins Bassoon and Piccolo lose their normal spatial relationship. TULP1 binds the ribbon protein RIBEYE, an interaction needed to keep the ribbon intact. These defects precede photoreceptor degeneration and are not seen in the rd10 mouse, which degenerates at a similar rate, so they are specific to TULP1 loss rather than a consequence of dying photoreceptors.

nodes.description: Before degeneration, rhodopsin and cone opsins accumulate ectopically in the inner segment plasma membrane of Tulp1-null photoreceptors instead of reaching the outer segment. Peripherin/RDS is delivered normally, so the defect is selective for the opsin carrier pathway. Rab8 and Rab11, two rhodopsin transport proteins, are also abnormally distributed, which points to a role in vesicle docking and fusion near the connecting cilium. The knock-in Tulp1 F492L tubby-domain allele and zebrafish tulp1a/tulp1b knockouts reproduce the opsin mislocalization.

nodes.description: The only disease-directed approach tested. Subretinal AAV2/5 delivery of Tulp1 under a photoreceptor (rhodopsin kinase) promoter at postnatal days 2 to 3 restored Tulp1 mRNA and protein to wild-type levels in Tulp1-null photoreceptors but did not preserve the outer nuclear layer and gave only a small, transient ERG benefit at one dose. Non-photoreceptor TULP1 expression is one proposed reason. No human trial has been reported.

evidence.reference_title: AAV-Delivered Tulp1 Supplementation Therapy Targeting Photoreceptors Provides Minimal Benefit in Tulp1-/- Retinas.
evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that TULP1 was expressed in photoreceptors; achieved levels of Tulp1 mRNA and protein were similar to wild type levels at p20.

evidence.reference_title: AAV-Delivered Tulp1 Supplementation Therapy Targeting Photoreceptors Provides Minimal Benefit in Tulp1-/- Retinas.
evidence.snippet: However, the thickness of the outer nuclear layer (ONL) did not improve in treated Tulp1-/- mice.

evidence.reference_title: AAV-Delivered Tulp1 Supplementation Therapy Targeting Photoreceptors Provides Minimal Benefit in Tulp1-/- Retinas.
evidence.snippet: Our results indicate that Tulp1 supplementation in photoreceptors may not be sufficient to provide robust benefit in Tulp1-/- mice.

nodes.description: Two knock-in lines carrying orthologs of human homozygous missense alleles. F492L, in the tubby domain, reproduces the null phenotype; D89Y, outside the tubby domain, keeps normal retinal morphology and function to 12 months.
nodes.id: Tulp1 F492L and D89Y knock-in mice

evidence.reference_title: TULP1 missense mutations cause variable retinal phenotypes and activation of the endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathway.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, these abnormalities were not seen in the Tulp1D89Y model; indeed, retinal morphology and function was preserved up to 12 months

nodes.description: Targeted Tulp1-null mice develop early-onset, rapid rod and cone degeneration with opsin mislocalization, extracellular rhodopsin-laden vesicles, ribbon synapse defects and an active IRE1 unfolded protein response, but normal hearing and body weight, unlike tubby mice. The rate of photoreceptor loss depends on genetic background: a protective Mtap1a allele reduces it.

evidence.reference_title: An allele of microtubule-associated protein 1A (Mtap1a) reduces photoreceptor degeneration in Tulp1 and Tub Mutant Mice.
evidence.snippet: The protective Mtap1a(129P2/OlaHsd) allele was shown to reduce photoreceptor loss in both Tulp1(tm1Pjn/tm1Pjn) and Tub(tub/tub) mice.

evidence.reference_title: Retinal degeneration but not obesity is observed in null mutants of the tubby-like protein 1 gene.
evidence.snippet: However, in contrast to tubby mice, Tulp1 (-/-)mice exhibited normal hearing ability and, surprisingly, normal body weight

nodes.description: Rod and cone full-field ERGs are not detectable with standard methods. Microvolt-level cone responses can be present in some patients, and reduced, delayed cone responses can be recorded in early childhood before they too are lost.

evidence.reference_title: Novel TULP1 mutation causing leber congenital amaurosis or early onset retinal degeneration.
evidence.snippet: Both scotopic and photopic electroretinograms were nondetectable.

evidence.reference_title: Tubby-like protein 1 homozygous splice-site mutation causes early-onset severe retinal degeneration.
evidence.snippet: Rod and cone electroretinograms (ERGs) were not detectable using standard methods; microvolt-level cone ERGs were present in some patients.

nodes.description: Kinetic fields are relatively wide in younger patients and shrink to peripheral islands in older patients.

evidence.reference_title: Tubby-like protein 1 homozygous splice-site mutation causes early-onset severe retinal degeneration.
evidence.snippet: Younger patients had a relatively wide extent of kinetic visual fields; older patients had only peripheral islands.

nodes.description: Homozygous frameshift allele in 16 Finnish patients with infantile or early-childhood onset.

evidence.reference_title: Natural history and biomarkers of retinal dystrophy caused by the biallelic TULP1 variant c.148delG.
evidence.snippet: The biallelic TULP1 variant c.148delG was associated with infantile and early childhood onset IRD.

evidence.reference_title: The genetic aetiology of retinal degeneration in children in Finland - new founder mutations identified.
evidence.snippet: Several founder mutations were detected including three novel founder mutations c.148delG in TULP1, c.2314C>R (p.Gln772Ter) in RPGRIP1 and c.533G>A (Trp178Ter) in TYR.

nodes.description: Homozygous nonsense founder allele on a shared haplotype in ten Arabian children with congenital rod-cone dystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: A TULP1 founder mutation, p.Gln301*, underlies a recognisable congenital rod-cone dystrophy phenotype on the Arabian Peninsula.
evidence.snippet: A specific haplotype was associated with p.Gln301* and was not present in controls.

nodes.description: Zebrafish have two TULP1 paralogs; tulp1a loss affects UV cones and tulp1b loss affects rods. The double knockout mislocalizes opsins in all photoreceptor types, shortens photoreceptor cilia and degenerates very early, with changes suggestive of ferroptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Tulp1 deficiency causes early-onset retinal degeneration through affecting ciliogenesis and activating ferroptosis in zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: knockout of tulp1b resulted in mislocalization of rod opsins and rod-cone degeneration
